issues.failure_explanation: In the stability estimate applied to \xih, \|(\xih^-)'(0)\| is the weakly imposed initial-velocity datum of the method that \xih satisfies. In the error equation at n=1, the jump conventions are: \jump{e_h'}(0) = e_h'(0^+) - (u_1-u_{0h}) (method convention), and (3.10) uses \jump{(\Pcalpbftt w)'}(0) = (\Pcalpbftt w)'(0^+) - w'(0), i.e., datum \PihEcal u_1 for w = \PihEcal u. Hence \jump{\xih'}(0) = \xih'(0^+) - (\PihEcal u_1 - \uoneh), so the correct datum is (\xih^-)'(0) = \PihEcal u_1 - \uoneh. The proof instead asserts it equals \uoneh - (\Pcalpbftt\PihEcal u)'(0^+), which is \jump{e_h'}(0) + \xih'(0^+) - a different quantity; the displayed chain of equalities is false in general.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the datum by \PihEcal u_1 - \uoneh and estimate it via the triangle inequality, the commutation (I-\PihEcal)(\Pcalpbftt u)'(0) = (\Pcalpbftt(I-\PihEcal)u)'(0), and the standard L^2-stability of the elliptic projection on quasi-uniform meshes (consistent with the paper's mesh assumptions); the lemma's stated right-hand side then still dominates, and no statement changes.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of Lemma 3.4 does not establish the stated estimate as written. The statement survives: with the correct datum, \|\PihEcal u_1 - \uoneh\|^2 \le 2\|u_1-\uoneh\|^2 + 2\|(I-\PihEcal)u_1\|^2, and (I-\PihEcal)u_1 = (I-\PihEcal)(u_1 - (\Pcalpbftt u)'(0)) + (\Pcalpbftt(I-\PihEcal)u)'(0), so the L^2-stability of \PihEcal bounds it by the lemma's own \|u_1-(\Pcalpbftt u)'(0)\| and \|(\Pcalpbftt(I-\PihEcal)u)'(0)\| terms; Theorems 3.5 and 3.6 (and hence the corollary) then go through unchanged.
issues.title: Wrong initial velocity datum identified for the \xih-problem in the proof of Lemma 3.4
issues.why_classification: The repair is a short, local correction of one proof step using a standard stability property; every substantive statement (the lemma and all downstream results) survives verbatim.

issues.failure_explanation: For u_0 in H^{s+1/2}, the elliptic-projection error in the H^1-seminorm satisfies |u_0 - \PihEcal u_0|_1 \lesssim h^{\min(\px,s-1/2)} \px^{-(s-1/2)} \|u_0\|_{s+1/2}: the h-exponent is \min(\px+1, s+1/2) - 1 = \min(\px, s-1/2). The proof and the theorem statement claim h^{\min(\px+1, s-1/2)}, i.e., one extra power of h whenever s - 1/2 > \px (e.g., for \px = 2 and smooth u_0 the claim is O(h^3) for an H^1 error that is only O(h^2), which is sharp). The companion term \gimel_2 uses the same exponent formula, but there it is correct because it is an L^2-error at regularity s-1/2; elsewhere in the same proof the H^1-estimates correctly use exponents \min(\px+1,\cdot)-1.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace \min(\px+1, s-1/2) by \min(\px, s-1/2) in the \gimel_1 term, both in (3.34) and in the statement of Theorem 3.6.
issues.overall_effect: The first term of the a priori estimate in Theorem 3.6 overstates the spatial convergence order by one in the saturated regime s - 1/2 > \px. Downstream results are unaffected: with the corrected exponent the term is still O(\tau^{2p}) in Corollary 3.7's smooth case, and for s \le \p the exponent coincides with the claimed one.
issues.title: One-order overestimate of the H^1 elliptic-projection rate in the \gimel_1 term of Theorem 3.6
issues.why_classification: A forced, local one-exponent correction in a single term; all advertised convergence rates and downstream statements survive.

issues.failure_explanation: For s \le p with h = O(\tau) and \alpha = 1, Theorem 3.6 bounds the squared error by a sum whose dominant terms are \gimel_5 and \gimel_6, both O(\tau^{2(s-1)}) when the norms appearing in the theorem are O(1): their exponents are 2\min(s-1, p+1) = 2(s-1) and 2\min(p+1, s-1) - 2(1-\alpha) = 2(s-1). Hence Theorem 3.6 yields only a O(\tau^{s-1}) error bound, whereas (3.35) claims O(\tau^{s-1/2}), half an order more. The given proof addresses only the smooth case (s \ge p+2, rate \tau^p); no argument for the singular case is presented. Obtaining \tau^{s-1/2} requires a per-term re-analysis with higher regularity indices for \gimel_5, \gimel_6 (e.g., \Delta u in H^{s+1}(0,T;L^2) and u'' in L^2(0,T;H^{s+1})), i.e., extra spatial regularity hypotheses that the corollary does not state.
